judged_text: Salesforce refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com instead of through refreshOAuthTokens, so when credential sharing is enabled the response is parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema, which strips id/issued_at/instance_url/signature/scope/token_type from the key persisted at the prisma.credential.update on lines 96-99. In sharing mode the first refresh stores a Salesforce credential lacking instance_url (the field ExtendedTokenResponse exists to carry), so subsequent loads build the jsforce connection without the instance URL and API calls go to the default login host and fail, while the parent application never sees Salesforce refresh traffic at all — the sync feature silently does not apply to Salesforce.

adjudication.rationale: In the Salesforce integration, the token refresh is implemented as a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper that routes refreshes through `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is on (contrast with Google/Office365/Zoom/etc in the diff). Therefore, when credential sharing is enabled, Salesforce refresh traffic will still go directly to Salesforce and the parent sync endpoint is never invoked, so the new sync feature does not apply to Salesforce. Additionally, Salesforce uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which in sharing mode switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (see `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`), so the data persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }}})` may omit Salesforce-specific fields (e.g., `instance_url`) needed by jsforce, depending on how the minimum schema parses/strips extra keys.
